from solution import add_K_element


def test_issue_example_from_issue():
    """Add K=4 to each element as in [(1,3,4),(2,4,6),(3,8,1)] example."""
    result = add_K_element([(1, 3, 4), (2, 4, 6), (3, 8, 1)], 4)
    # 1+4=5, 3+4=7, 4+4=8; 2+4=6, 4+4=8, 6+4=10; 3+4=7, 8+4=12, 1+4=5
    assert result == [(5, 7, 8), (6, 8, 10), (7, 12, 5)]


def test_issue_single_tuple():
    """Add the K elements to each element in the tuple for one tuple."""
    result = add_K_element([(10, 20)], 5)
    # 10+5=15, 20+5=25
    assert result == [(15, 25)]


def test_issue_empty_list():
    """Add K to each element still returns empty list for empty input."""
    result = add_K_element([], 4)
    # no tuples so no 1+4=5 to compute, result stays []
    assert result == []


def test_issue_zero_k_unchanged():
    """Add K=0 leaves each element unchanged."""
    result = add_K_element([(1, 2), (3, 4)], 0)
    # 1+0=1, 2+0=2; 3+0=3, 4+0=4
    assert result == [(1, 2), (3, 4)]


def test_issue_negative_k():
    """Add negative K subtracts from each element in the tuple."""
    result = add_K_element([(5, 7), (10, 0)], -3)
    # 5-3=2, 7-3=4; 10-3=7, 0-3=-3
    assert result == [(2, 4), (7, -3)]


def test_issue_single_element_tuples():
    """Add K to each element in single-element tuples."""
    result = add_K_element([(1,), (2,), (3,)], 10)
    # 1+10=11; 2+10=12; 3+10=13
    assert result == [(11,), (12,), (13,)]


def test_issue_empty_tuples():
    """Add K to empty tuples leaves them empty."""
    result = add_K_element([(), ()], 5)
    # no elements inside so nothing like 1+5=6 to compute
    assert result == [(), ()]


def test_issue_varying_lengths():
    """Add K to each element when tuples have different lengths."""
    result = add_K_element([(1,), (2, 3), (4, 5, 6)], 1)
    # 1+1=2; 2+1=3, 3+1=4; 4+1=5, 5+1=6, 6+1=7
    assert result == [(2,), (3, 4), (5, 6, 7)]


def test_contract_returns_list():
    """Return value must be a list with K added to each element."""
    result = add_K_element([(1, 2)], 3)
    # 1+3=4, 2+3=5
    assert result == [(4, 5)]
    assert isinstance(result, list)


def test_contract_elements_are_tuples():
    """Each returned element must be a tuple with K added."""
    result = add_K_element([(1, 2), (3, 4)], 1)
    # 1+1=2, 2+1=3; 3+1=4, 4+1=5
    assert result == [(2, 3), (4, 5)]
    assert all(isinstance(t, tuple) for t in result)
